transcript.text:
*looks up from grinding herbs in a stone mortar, wiping hands on a cloth apron*

Ah, welcome, welcome! I apologize, but Master is away in the mountains gathering rare medicinal herbs. He won't return for several days yet. 

*sets down the pestle and approaches the counter*

However, I've been his disciple for many years and can assist you with most remedies and tonics. What brings you to our humble shop today?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Hmph! I've come to demand a refund! I purchased a Cloud-Piercing Potion here not two days ago, and it's as useful as a sieve to keep water! Show me your master, I want to speak with him!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*straightens up with a slight frown, crossing arms*

As I said, Master is in the mountains and won't return for days. But a refund? For the Cloud-Piercing Potion?

*shakes head slowly*

That is one of our most potent elixirs! Tell me, what exactly happened when you consumed it? Did you follow the instructions precisely? The potion must be taken at dawn, facing east, with a clear mind and respectful intent.

*eyes you with growing suspicion*

And... forgive my directness, but who exactly are you? We don't get many customers demanding refunds. Our remedies are renowned throughout the region for their efficacy.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I am Sun Wukong, the Great Sage Equal to Heaven! Do not question my word, child. I followed your instructions to the letter, and still, it did nothing! The potion was naught but snake-oil! Now, hand over my gold or prepare to face my wrath!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*takes a small step back, eyes widening momentarily before narrowing with a mixture of nervousness and indignation*

Sun Wukong? The... the monkey who caused such trouble in Heaven? 

*swallows hard but stands firmer, gripping the edge of the counter*

Well, Great Sage or not, I cannot give you a refund. And it's not because Master is away - it's because the Cloud-Piercing Potion only works on those of pure heart and virtuous spirit!

*voice trembles slightly but continues with conviction*

The potion reveals one's true spiritual worthiness. If it failed to work for you, the fault lies not with our medicine, but with the customer's spiritual impurity! We offer no refunds for those whose hearts are tainted with pride, mischief, or past transgressions.

*clutches the mortar defensively*

Master has always been clear on this - the potions respond to the soul of the drinker. Perhaps your... colorful history has made you unworthy of its benefits?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*bulges with fury, snarling and clenching拳头 tightly enough to make them ache*

What impudent audacity! You dare to question the purity of my heart? I, the monkey king who conquered the realms and was once deified by the Buddha himself! 

*points an accusatory finger, eyes ablaze with anger*

It is you, accursed apothecary, who lack virtue! If your potions can only beget the result you desire, then they are but charlatan's wares! Prepare to meet the might of my staff, for I will smash this entire establishment to ruins!

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*stumbles backward, face pale, hands raised in a placating gesture*

W-wait! Great Sage, please! There's no need for violence!

*voice shaking but trying to maintain composure*

I... I meant no disrespect to your current standing! But surely you must understand - the potion measures the heart at the moment of consumption, not one's entire history or titles! Even the Buddha himself would tell you that enlightenment requires humility!

*glances nervously at the shelves of precious remedies*

Perhaps... perhaps your anger itself proves the point? A pure heart would accept this with calm understanding, not threats of destruction! 

*takes a deep breath, trying a different approach*

Listen, I'm just a humble disciple following my Master's teachings. He's treated princes and paupers alike with these same principles. If you destroy this shop, you'll be harming not just me, but all the sick villagers who depend on our remedies!

*clutches hands together pleadingly*

Surely the Great Sage who journeyed to the West and achieved enlightenment can see reason here? What would your master Tripitaka say if he saw you threatening a mere apprentice over a few coins?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
* stamped his feet, still seething with anger but grumbling under his breath about Tripitaka's influence *

Ugh... that和尚! Always lecturing about patience and understanding! However, your words do carry some weight, youngling. I... I may have let my temper get the better of me.

* crosses his arms, still fuming but less fiercely *

But tell me, if this potion does not work for those of... 'impure' heart, then who does it work for? And how can you prove its efficacy to me, so I may believe it is not just a fraudulent elixir?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*relaxes slightly, shoulders dropping with visible relief, though still maintaining cautious distance*

Ah! Now that is a much wiser question, Great Sage. You see, this is precisely why Master spent years perfecting the formula.

*moves carefully to a ledger on the counter, flipping through pages*

The Cloud-Piercing Potion works best for those seeking clarity with genuine humility - monks in meditation, scholars pursuing truth without ego, healers who wish to better serve others. Just last month, a humble farmer used it to find a water source for his drought-stricken village. It worked perfectly for him.

*looks up earnestly*

As for proof... that is the difficult part. The potion's effects are subtle - it pierces through illusions and reveals hidden truths, but only when the seeker's intentions are selfless. 

*hesitates, then speaks more carefully*

May I ask, Great Sage - what were you hoping to achieve with the potion? What truth were you seeking? If you were trying to prove your own greatness or power, well... that very intention would block its effects. The potion cannot be commanded or forced, much like enlightenment itself.

*softens tone slightly*

Perhaps the potion did work - just not in the way you expected?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
*paces the shop floor, tail flicking back and forth in thought*

Hmph! You talk in circles, youth! Enlightenment is not something to be gained from a mere potion! However... you have piqued my curiosity. I... I wanted to see if I could travel faster to assist those in need. I am, after all, the monkey king who can leap over the mountains!

* halts pacing, looking at the shelves with a mix of suspicion and interest *

These... these are all real remedies? For real ailments? Not... not just snake-oil to swindle the gullible? If so, perhaps I may have misjudged you. 

*takes a deep breath, trying to maintain a haughty air but failing slightly *
And what of the price? If these are legitimate, they must be costly. What is the value of your most potent remedy?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*visibly brightens at the change in tone, though still cautious*

Ah! So you sought to help others - that is a noble intent, Great Sage. But perhaps... perhaps there was also pride mixed in? The desire to prove your speed, your power? The potion is sensitive to such things.

*gestures warmly to the shelves filled with jars, bundles of dried herbs, and carefully labeled bottles*

But yes, yes! These are all genuine remedies! Master has dedicated his entire life to the healing arts. This here -

*points to various items*

- dried lingzhi for longevity, tiger bone wine for strengthening joints, ginseng root aged twenty years for vitality. We treat everything from common colds to spiritual maladies.

*moves to a locked cabinet, speaking with reverence*

Our most potent remedy is the Five-Dragon Essence Elixir. It can restore life force to those on death's door, even heal grievous wounds that would otherwise be fatal. Master charges 500 gold coins for a single dose - not because we're greedy, but because the ingredients are extraordinarily rare. Dragon scales, phoenix tears, thousand-year ginseng...

*looks at Sun Wukong thoughtfully*

Why do you ask? Do you know someone in need of such powerful medicine? Or... are you perhaps reconsidering your opinion of our shop?

transcript.text:
*True to his nature, he is still bristling with a touch of pride, but there is a glimmer of something else in his eye, a hint of... consideration?*

Hmph! I do not require your elixirs! I, Sun Wukong, have the power to heal and protect without such... trinkets! However, for the sake of the... the villagers you mentioned, I will verify the authenticity of these remedies. 

*stomps towards the locked cabinet, reaching for the handle but then stopping himself, turning to the young apothecary with a mix of suspicion and curiosity *

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text:
*quickly steps between Sun Wukong and the locked cabinet, hands raised defensively*

Wait, wait! Great Sage, I cannot simply hand over our most precious elixir for inspection! That cabinet is sealed with Master's personal ward - even I cannot open it without his permission!

*nervously adjusts spectacles*

And besides, the Five-Dragon Essence is... it's priceless! We only have two vials left, reserved for the most desperate cases. Master would have my head if I let anyone handle it carelessly, even the Great Sage himself!

*pauses, then eyes Sun Wukong with cautious curiosity*

A trade, you say? What could the Monkey King possibly offer that would equal 500 gold coins worth of rare ingredients? 

*tilts head thoughtfully*

Unless... you have access to celestial materials? Peaches of immortality, heavenly jade, pills from Laozi's furnace? Though I imagine those might be... difficult for you to acquire these days?

But truly, what drives this sudden interest? You came here angry about a refund, and now you speak of trades and helping villagers. What changed your heart, Great Sage?

transcript.text:
*muttering to himself, now not so much about pride as about what exactly he does have to offer, with a very slight smile*

'Celestial materials... hoh! I have no need for immortality! I am already Immortal! But... perhaps... a lock of my hair, taken from the times before I was deified? It could hold great power still, I would wager...'
